wordHints.Ball-jointed: Think of articulated figures with movable limbs — a specific type of collectible doll prized by artists and photographers.
wordHints.Bobblehead: These novelty items have an oversized head on a spring — a toy or collectible figure, not a traditional doll but firmly in the doll family.
wordHints.Voodoo: Associated with folk magic, this type uses pins and is meant to represent a person — a doll by name and by form.
wordHints.Russian nesting (Matryoshka): The Matryoshka is the iconic wooden figure that opens to reveal smaller figures inside — a traditional decorative doll from Russia.
wordHints.Barbie: The world's most famous fashion doll — this one should confirm the category immediately if you spot it.

fullAnalysis: The five clues for Pinpoint #682 — Ball-jointed, Bobblehead, Voodoo, Russian nesting (Matryoshka), and Barbie — all point to the same category: Types of doll.

Ball-jointed dolls are poseable collectibles with articulated limbs connected by internal stringing, popular with artists and hobbyists. Bobbleheads are novelty figures with spring-mounted oversized heads, sold as sports memorabilia and pop-culture collectibles. Voodoo dolls come from folk magic traditions and are used symbolically to represent a person. The Russian nesting doll, or Matryoshka, is a traditional wooden figure that splits open to reveal a series of progressively smaller dolls inside. Barbie is the iconic fashion doll introduced by Mattel in 1959.
The unifying answer is Types of doll. Each clue names a distinct variety — collectible, novelty, folk, traditional, and fashion — making this a broad but consistent category.
solutionNarrative: I spotted Barbie immediately and guessed the category was something doll-related. I ran through the others: Voodoo doll, Bobblehead doll, Matryoshka doll, Ball-jointed doll. Every single clue fit. The answer is Types of doll.
